prompt:
Create a coordinated TripLOG expense UI mockup with two complete, readable screens side by side: a wide expense ledger and a narrower expense-entry panel. Preserve TripLOG’s pink wordmark, lemon-yellow primary actions, pale-blue secondary accents, white surfaces and dark-navy text. Use restrained borders, generous spacing, clear Korean typography and consistent outline icons.

Ledger: “지출 기록”, “오사카·교토 가족여행”, compact “영수증” and “+ 지출 추가” actions. One budget summary shows “총 지출 2,354,695원”, “남은 예산 1,145,305원”, “전체 예산 3,500,000원” and a thin 67% progress bar. Below, show search, category filter and latest-first sorting, compact “전체 / 사전구매 / 여행 중” tabs, and aligned expense rows with date, description, category, payment method, right-aligned amount and an edit icon. Use travel expenses such as accommodation, flights and airport trains. Make descriptions readable without competing with amounts. Retain bottom navigation “개요 / 일정 / 지출 / 리포트 / 더보기”.

Entry panel: “지출 추가”, close button and compact “영수증” action. Put one prominent editable “결제 금액” field first, showing “2,800” with a “JPY · 엔” selector and “약 26,600원 · 100엔 = 950원” underneath. Then “내용” with “이치란 라멘 점심”, six compact category choices “식비 / 교통 / 숙소 / 관광 / 쇼핑 / 기타”, paired “여행 일정” and “결제일” controls, “카드 / 현금”, and a collapsed “메모 · 결제한 사람” section. Keep “저장 후 계속” and yellow “지출 저장” actions visible at the bottom. Design usable, responsive app screens that can be faithfully implemented in HTML and CSS.
